items.q: How do I know the loader matches today’s Apex Legends client?
items.a: Open cheatsapexlegends.org/status after any client or Javelin change. Treat yesterday’s GREEN note as stale—do not inject until today’s label lists your build.
items.aHtml: Open status after any client or Javelin change. Treat yesterday’s GREEN note as stale—do not inject until today’s label lists your build.

items.q: What arrives in the portal after checkout?
items.a: You get the Windows loader for the SKU you paid for. Tune Player ESP, aim, and loot tabs, then save a profile. Keep HVCI, core isolation, TPM, and secure boot enabled.

items.q: Is a ban still possible while using the menu?
items.a: Yes. Javelin can flag accounts even on conservative presets. This site does not promise a clean session.

items.q: Hardware flag vs account ban—which is which?
items.a: When only new logins fail on one tower but work elsewhere, suspect a hardware flag. That is what the separate HWID Spoofer key is for. Account-only penalties are not fixed by spoofing, and lifetime on the menu never bundles the spoofer.

items.q: What machine do I need before I buy?
items.a: Windows 10 or 11 64-bit with HVCI, core isolation, TPM, and secure boot enabled, plus the current Apex Legends PC client. Consoles, macOS, and Linux are out of scope.

items.q: Can I transfer my license to a friend’s PC?
items.a: Email support from the purchase address. Keys are not free-floating transfers—persistent hardware blocks need the spoofer checkout, not a courtesy move.

items.q: Which products share one cart?
items.a: None. the menu and the HWID Spoofer are separate line items on the products page. The menu is $35 for 31 days or $150 lifetime. The HWID spoofer is $50 for 31 days or $150 lifetime.

items.q: Does menu lifetime cover the HWID spoofer?
items.a: No. A $150 lifetime key is only for the Apex hack menu. Spoofer lifetime is its own $150 checkout, with a $50 monthly option. Shorter menu time does not roll into lifetime credit.

items.q: What should I expect from Player ESP squads?
items.a: Tagged legends show names, teams, and rough position in your FOV. Add Distance ESP when rotating third parties; trim label count if fights get noisy.

items.q: First-night Advanced Aimbot settings?
items.a: Keep FOV tight, smoothing high, and visibility checks on. Log a few firing-range drills before ranked, then widen FOV only if tracking feels sluggish.

items.q: When does Weapon ESP pay off?
items.a: It prints the opponent’s gun above their box so you know whether to slide in or hold range. Disable it if you already run full skeleton and box clutter.

items.q: How should I use Health Bar in ring fights?
items.a: Bars stack shield pips and health on tagged players. Drop skeleton thickness or raise distance cutoffs when multiple teams collapse in one POI.

items.q: Loot ESP during zone crunch—worth it?
items.a: Yes for death boxes and ground swaps between rotations. Tier filters stop grey guns from covering enemies during endgame scans.

items.q: No Recoil vs manual control?
items.a: The module trims vertical climb on sustained beams. It will not fix whiffed flicks—dial aimbot first, then add light recoil assist for AR/LMG sprays.

items.q: What is EA Javelin Bypass on cheatsapexlegends.org?
items.a: It means builds are checked against live Javelin before the status note goes GREEN. RED still means wait. It is engineering fit, not a ban waiver.

items.q: Will Stream Proof hide overlays on stream?
items.a: It hides menu and ESP from common capture paths while you see them locally. GPU driver, dual-PC, and OBS scene setups still need a private test.

items.q: Fastest way to reach 24/7 Support?
items.a: Use the Discord invite on the support page with order email, product (menu vs spoofer), and a screenshot of any loader error text.

items.q: Buy the HWID spoofer when…
items.a: Choose HWID Spoofer if brand-new accounts lock to one desktop but succeed on a laptop. It will not lift an account-only sanction on the same iron.

items.q: Do I need a DMA board for this key?
items.a: No. Checkout delivers a software loader for your own Windows box. DMA hardware is a different SKU and is not included here.

items.q: Do blog posts override the product page list?
items.a: Guides walk through ideas and link back to the menu. Module names on that product card beat anything written in an article.

items.q: Article steps fail—what should I send support?
items.a: Paste the guide title, your receipt email, and the loader message verbatim. Screenshots beat paraphrasing.

items.q: Are tutorial sliders safe after a Javelin push?
items.a: Assume presets age overnight. Read status, then import your saved profile instead of transcribing numbers from the post.

items.q: 31-day or lifetime for a first purchase?
items.a: Pick 31 days to sample one SKU. The menu is $35 for 31 days or $150 lifetime. The HWID spoofer is $50 for 31 days or $150 lifetime. Credits from a short plan never apply to lifetime, and lifetime on one SKU never unlocks the others.

items.q: Can I turn a 31-day key into lifetime later?
items.a: Lifetime is a fresh checkout on the same product. Prior $35 or $50 payments are not discounted toward the $150 lifetime price.

items.q: My 31-day window ended—now what?
items.a: Access stops at day 31 unless you buy another window or lifetime on that exact product. Lifetime never auto-renews and keys do not hop between products.

items.q: Refunds if I bought the wrong plan?

updates.title: Ranked enforcement after the Cipher patch
updates.summary: After the Season 31 Cipher patch, Respawn suspended 906 accounts for up to 365 days. The cases were a matchmaking exploit that skipped Ranked entry costs. That wave is an account suspension. It is not a confirmed ID ban. In most cases there is no ID ban.

updates.title: Season 31 on live servers
updates.summary: Season 31 added Strongholds (loot bunkers a squad can capture), Akimbo Wingmans on heavy ammo, a Crypto rework with a full-circle drone scan, and Legend bans before the match in Diamond and above. A client shift like that makes a note from an older build stale. Read this page again before you load.

updates.title: PC anti-cheat moved to EA Javelin
updates.summary: Respawn replaced Easy Anti-Cheat on PC with EA Javelin Anticheat. EA describes it as aimed at kernel-level cheats and other third-party software, and cites an accuracy rate above 99%. That figure is their claim. It is not a confirmed ID ban, and it is not a claim that a file bypasses easily. In most cases there is no ID ban. A GREEN label here is still only the current file check.

updates.title: Adapters and recoil scripts banned
updates.summary: External input adapters (Cronus, XIM, Titan, Strikepack) and recoil-cancel scripts (jitter macros and RC filters) are against publisher rules on PC and console. Reports on those tools are behavior flags. They are not a confirmed ID ban. In most cases there is no ID ban.

updates.title: Windows security baseline
updates.summary: Supported builds keep HVCI, core isolation, TPM, and secure boot enabled. Turning them off for a loader is a common support failure, not a fix for a RED status label.
